The Cow has 8 Hitpoints, max hit 1 (crush melee), 4-tick attack speed, and Defence level 1 (all defence bonuses -21).
Cows are 100% resistant to poison and venom and have no elemental weakness.
Cow calves and dairy cows also count toward the task.
No required protective item and no task extension unlock exist for Cows.

A trivial low-level Slayer-XP task: kill Cows in the Lumbridge cow field or Falador farm with any melee weapon. Cows have very low Defence and barely fight back, so no food or special gear is needed; collect cowhide for a little profit while completing the streak.

cow-field.name: Cow fields (Lumbridge/Falador)
notes: Cows are densest in the Lumbridge cow field (east of Lumbridge Castle) and the Falador farm; the Crafting Guild also has cows. There is no single canonical cow location for a slayer task, so multi, cannon and safespot are conservative defaults and not wiki-confirmed for one spot.
Cows cluster densely in the Lumbridge cow field and Falador farm, but no single canonical spawn count is wiki-stated (honest UNKNOWN), so no amount overlay is authored.
Cows drop cowhide, making this a mildly profitable starter Slayer-XP task.

crabs.name: Crabs
notes: Crabs require only Slayer level 1 with no combat or quest requirement to be assigned by Mazchna, Vannaka, or Chaeldar.

Assignment data verified 2026-07-03 against the raw wikitext of Slayer task/Crabs (pageid 574430): Mazchna 30-50, Vannaka 40-90, Chaeldar 70-130, each weighting 8; no extended amounts (task extensions are N/A for all three masters).
slayerTargetId 154 is the 'id' field from the Slayer task/Crabs infobox.

Counting variants: Rock Crab, Sand Crab, Ammonite Crab, Frost Crab, Swamp Crab, King Sand Crab, Giant Rock Crab, and the Mogre Camp Crab. The Gemstone Crab and hermit crabs do NOT count toward the task.

All crabs use the Crush attack style and are low-damage; most need no special gear. Crabs appear as inactive 'rocks' and emerge when a player stands adjacent, becoming aggressive until the 10-minute tolerance timer expires, after which aggression is reset by leaving and returning.

Most crabs have a small earth-spell elemental weakness and negligible melee defence, so melee is the standard kill. Exceptions: Swamp Crabs resist melee/magic but have -55 ranged defence (use Ranged); Frost Crabs have a 100% fire-spell weakness; Giant Rock Crabs have very high melee/ranged defence and are best hit with earth spells.

King Sand Crabs and Giant Rock Crabs have much higher combat stats and are only advisable to kill on task when seeking their specific drops (e.g. rock-shell armour, Ancient shards, Dark totem pieces, medium clue scrolls).
No task extension unlock or related Slayer shop unlock exists for Crabs.
defaultVariantId is sand-crab: Sand Crabs are the most popular crab for the task, have no quest requirement, plentiful spawns across many locations, and negligible defence.

Crabs need only Slayer level 1, so any master (Mazchna, Vannaka, or Chaeldar) can assign them. For fast, no-requirement kills, use Sand Crabs (Crabclaw Isle, the Hosidius coast, or the Isle of Souls) or Rock Crabs north of Rellekka; Ammonite Crabs on Fossil Island (after Bone Voyage) give the most XP of the low-level crabs. Crabs appear as 'rocks' and emerge when you stand next to them, so reset their aggression by stepping a few tiles away and returning whenever they stop attacking. Kill the low-defence crabs with any melee weapon (a crush weapon or high-crush-defence armour helps if you take damage). Use Ranged on Swamp Crabs (negative ranged defence), fire spells on Frost Crabs (100% fire weakness), and only fight King Sand Crabs or Giant Rock Crabs if you want their specific drops, as they have much higher Defence and Hitpoints.

rock-crabs-rellekka.name: Rock Crabs (North of Rellekka)
notes: Rock Crabs are found on the coast directly north of Rellekka, with very plentiful spawn points; other spawns exist at Waterbirth Island, west of Mount Quidamortem, in the Waterbirth Island Dungeon, and in the Brine Rat Cavern. They appear as inactive 'rocks' until a player stands adjacent, then become aggressive; aggression must be reset by leaving and returning after 10 minutes.
Rock Crabs (level 13) with very plentiful spawns directly north of Rellekka; also at Waterbirth Island, west of Mount Quidamortem, and in the Brine Rat Cavern.
Appear as inactive 'rocks' until a player stands adjacent; aggression must be reset by leaving and returning after 10 minutes.

sand-crabs-crabclaw-isle.name: Sand Crabs (Crabclaw Isle / Hosidius coast)
notes: Sand Crabs have very plentiful spawn points across many areas: Crabclaw Isle, the Crabclaw Caves, the southern Hosidius coast, east of the Hosidius vinery, the Isle of Souls, the Avium Savannah, and Outer Fortis. They appear as inactive 'sandy rocks' until a player stands adjacent; aggression is reset by leaving and returning after the 10-minute tolerance timer.

Sand Crabs (level 15) with very plentiful spawns across Crabclaw Isle, the Crabclaw Caves, the southern Hosidius coast, east of the Hosidius vinery, the Isle of Souls, the Avium Savannah, and Outer Fortis.
The most popular modern crab for training and Slayer tasks; reset aggression by stepping away and returning.

ammonite-crabs-fossil-island.name: Ammonite Crabs (Fossil Island)
notes: Ammonite Crabs are found on Fossil Island, which requires completion of Bone Voyage to reach. They give more Slayer XP than the low-level training crabs (100 XP) and appear as 'Fossil Rocks' until a player stands adjacent; aggression is reset by leaving and returning after the tolerance timer.
Ammonite Crabs (level 25) on Fossil Island give 100 Slayer XP each, the most of the low-level crabs.
Requires completion of Bone Voyage to reach Fossil Island.

ruins-of-tapoyauik.name: Ruins of Tapoyauik
notes: Requires The Heart of Darkness. Contains 7 adult Blue dragons, 7 baby Blue dragons, and 5 Brutal blue dragons; charged Pendant of ates gives very fast access, and nearby moonlight moths can provide prayer.
Frost Crabs (level 15) with a 100% weakness to fire spells; requires partial completion of The Heart of Darkness.
Melee works fine, but fire spells are extremely effective.

haunted-woods.name: Haunted Woods
notes: Requires Priest in Peril. Fairy ring ALQ is in the middle of the woods; nearby leeches can drain stats and do not appear on the minimap.
Fairy ring ALQ is in the Haunted Woods (needs a Dramen or Lunar staff).
Swamp Crabs (level 55) in the Haunted Woods and at Slepe; they have high melee/magic defence but -55 ranged defence, so Ranged is best.
The Haunted Woods/Slepe area is not on the cannon-prohibited list and Swamp Crabs are targetable, so a cannon can be placed (unlike Sand/Ammonite Crabs, which cannons ignore).

catacombs-of-kourend.name: Catacombs of Kourend
notes: Black demons here can be safespotted and give access to Ancient shards and Dark totem pieces, but their higher Defence makes them an inefficient Black demons task option. Mutated bloodvelds appear in three groups, can be safespotted, and use the Catacombs drop table including ancient shards and dark totem pieces. Brutal blue dragons here are safespottable, cannot be cannoned, and can drop ancient shards and Dark totem parts. Hellhounds here are multicombat, safespottable, cannot be cannoned, and can reset aggression by running south and up the vine to the Giants' Den.
Xeric's Heart (Xeric's talisman) is beside the Catacombs entrance.
King Sand Crabs (level 107) give the most Slayer XP per kill (200) but have high Hitpoints and Defence.
Can drop Ancient shards, Dark totem pieces, and medium clue scrolls; best killed on task mainly for those drops.

waterbirth-island-dungeon.name: Waterbirth Island Dungeon
notes: The Waterbirth Island Dungeon holds the level 137 Giant Rock Crab (kill only for drops such as rock-shell armour and medium clue scrolls, as it has very high Defence) as well as ordinary Rock Crabs. Reaching the island uses the Rellekka boat or fairy ring; deeper Dagannoth areas need extra preparation.
Giant Rock Crabs (level 137) have very high Defence; only worth killing on task for drops such as rock-shell armour pieces or medium clue scrolls.
Magic (earth spells) is the least-resisted style against them.

mogre-camp.name: Mogre Camp
notes: The Mogre Camp holds level 21/23 Crabs and requires partial completion of Recipe for Disaster (Freeing Pirate Pete) to access. Conservative multi, cannon and safespot defaults are used as they are not wiki-confirmed here.
Crabs (levels 21/23) require partial completion of Recipe for Disaster (Freeing Pirate Pete) to access the Mogre Camp.
Low Slayer XP (18/19) compared with Sand or Ammonite Crabs.

crawling-hands.name: Crawling Hands
notes: Crawling Hands require 5 Slayer and Priest in Peril (for Slayer Tower access) to be assigned by Turael, Spria, or Mazchna.
slayerTargetId 285 is SYNTHETIC (c2-c3-worklist section 1 allocation contract); the real SLAYER_TARGET varp value is a QA live-verify item.
All Crawling Hand variants share 15 Hitpoints, max hit 1 (crush), 4-tick attack speed, and Defence level 3.
Crawling Hands are undead: the salve amulet and Crumble Undead both apply.
They have no elemental weakness; any melee weapon clears them trivially.
No required protective item and no task extension unlock exist for Crawling Hands.

A trivial starter task: kill the ground-floor Crawling Hands with any melee weapon. They have max hit 1 and 15 Hitpoints, so no protection prayers or special gear are needed; a salve amulet gives a small undead damage bonus.

slayer-tower.name: Slayer Tower
notes: Bloodvelds on the first floor can be safespotted and receive additional Slayer experience from completed Morytania Diary tiers; other Slayer Tower tasks may have different floor-specific mechanics.
Fairy ring CKS is beside the Slayer Tower (needs a Dramen or Lunar staff).
24 Crawling Hand spawns of levels 8 and 12 on the ground floor.
A cannon cannot be placed anywhere in the Slayer Tower (a strange magical force blocks setup), so this task is not cannonable.

crocodiles.name: Crocodiles
notes: Crocodiles are assigned only by Vannaka at 40-90 per task with a weighting of 6; there is no task extension.
The assignment gate is combat level 50 only (no Slayer level, no quest); the monsters themselves are combat level 63.
There is no Slayer_task/Crocodiles wiki page (verified missing on 2026-07-03); task facts are taken from the Crocodile monster page (pageid 15028) and the master-supplied assignment data.
slayerTargetId is null because no task infobox with an 'id' field exists; the monster page exposes NPC ids 11581 (water), 11582 (land), and 4184 (water & land) rather than a Slayer target id.
Crocodiles have a 40% elemental weakness to earth spells; weakness.style is MAGIC/EARTH to reflect this, though their low melee defence (slash 12) makes any melee weapon effective as well.
Waterskins are strongly recommended but are not a worn entry gate, so requiredItemId and requiredItemName are left null.

Accept the task from Vannaka (combat level 50) and travel to the River Elid south of Pollnivneach. Earth spells hit nearly every cast thanks to the 40% earth weakness, and crocodiles can also be killed quickly with melee since their defence in every melee style is low. Because many crocodiles are water-bound, ranging or maging them from one tile back from the shore is safe and efficient; safespots west of Nardah and east of the Ruins of Unkah remove almost all incoming damage. Bring waterskins (and optionally desert clothing) for the heat, and recharge Prayer at the Nardah or Sophanem altars.

river-elid.name: River Elid (south of Pollnivneach)
notes: Crocodiles are found in the Kharidian Desert south of Pollnivneach on either side of the River Elid, with further spawns near the Ruins of Unkah, near the Ruins of Ullek, and (after Icthlarin's Little Helper) just north of Sophanem. Bring waterskins to survive the desert heat. Safespots exist: a cactus west of the magic carpet at Nardah covers two water spawns, and the wall east of the Ruins of Unkah covers others; the water-bound crocodiles can be ranged/maged from one tile back from the shore. Multi and cannon are not wiki-confirmed here, so conservative defaults are used.
Main concentration of spawns is south of Pollnivneach on either side of the River Elid; fighting on the south bank draws crocodiles across from the water and is less click-intensive.
Safespot two water spawns from the cactus west of the magic carpet at Nardah, or use the wall east of the Ruins of Unkah to negate food and waterskin needs.
The grassy area south of the Ruins of Ullek has 12 spawns and does not require waterskins if you stay near the water.
After Icthlarin's Little Helper, spawns just north of Sophanem allow long trips using the nearby altar and water sink.
Bring waterskins for the desert heat; Nardah (after Spirits of the Elid) and Sophanem altars recharge Prayer.

custodian-stalker.name: Custodian stalker
notes: Custodian stalkers require 54 Slayer and completion of Shadows of Custodia; Chaeldar assigns 70-130 at weight 11 and Nieve assigns 110-170 at weight 8.
The Un-restraining Order extension costs 100 Slayer reward points and increases assignments to 200-250.
The Stalker Den is the sole task location; do not reuse stalker-den-zygomites, which is the Ancient Zygomite tuned copy.
The Stalker Den has multicombat cannonable zones in the south-west, and single-combat caverns in the south-east and north.
Most damage is prevented with Protect from Melee, but the low-health spore special can cause bleed and may be blocked with Protect from Magic.
Gear with high magic defence such as dragonhide reduces the chance of taking damage from the special attack.
Players are encouraged to reach 76 Slayer for Elder custodian stalkers, which have better drops and are the only variant that can spawn Ancient Custodian.
Ranged multicombat with a dwarf multicannon and Venator bow is the first wiki equipment tab; magic multicombat and melee single-combat are alternatives.

slayerTargetId 244 is a synthetic placeholder per the WC-1..11 contract (240 + WC index); the real SLAYER_TARGET varp value for Custodian stalker is unverified and detection falls back to the RuneLite task-name path.

Use the Stalker Den's south-west multicombat cannonable area with ranged gear such as Venator bow, Protect from Melee, and prayer restoration; switch to magic multicombat or melee in single-combat caverns as preferred, and prioritise Elder custodian stalkers at 76 Slayer for superior spawns and better drops.

stalker-den-custodian-stalkers.name: Stalker Den
notes: Requires completion of Shadows of Custodia for full access. Custodian stalkers occupy multicombat cannonable zones in the south-west and single-combat caverns in the south-east and north; a safespot is documented for Elder custodian stalkers in a western single-combat area, so these flags describe supported zones rather than every tile.
The task page does not publish one combined spawn count for the family.
The Stalker Den has multicombat cannonable zones in the south-west and single-combat caverns in the south-east and north.
A safespot is documented for Elder custodian stalkers in the western single-combat area.

dagannoth.name: Dagannoth
notes: Dagannoth require 75 combat and completion of Horror from the Deep to be assigned.
They are known for high slayer experience rates and easy task completions.
The Lighthouse basement is a strong AFK choice and allows a dwarf cannon in multicombat.
Jormungand's Prison is a common cannon location after The Fremennik Exiles because all Dagannoth there use melee.
Catacombs of Kourend cannot be cannoned, but prayer-boosting melee gear and prayer potions allow AFK kills with Auto Retaliate.
Dinh's bulwark special attack with Lightbearer can refresh aggression in the Catacombs without leaving the area.
Waterbirth Island has stronger Dagannoth; dagannoth spawn can be triggered from nearby eggs while the monsters are still aggressive.
Dagannoth Kings are a rewarding alternative on a normal Dagannoth task or a Konar Waterbirth Island assignment.
80 Agility with a Summer pie boost or 85 Agility for shortcuts and Elite Fremennik Diary for noted Dagannoth bones make Dagannoth Kings much better.
Expert Reanimation on ensouled dagannoth heads can train Prayer during a task, but it lowers combat and Slayer experience rates.
Dagannoth frequently drop herb seeds, so bringing a seed box is recommended.
Use cannon + melee at the Lighthouse or Jormungand's Prison for fast tasks; use Catacombs prayer AFK for low effort; kill Dagannoth Kings for profit and Slayer helm bonuses when prepared.

catacombs-of-kourend.name: Catacombs of Kourend
notes: Black demons here can be safespotted and give access to Ancient shards and Dark totem pieces, but their higher Defence makes them an inefficient Black demons task option. Mutated bloodvelds appear in three groups, can be safespotted, and use the Catacombs drop table including ancient shards and dark totem pieces. Brutal blue dragons here are safespottable, cannot be cannoned, and can drop ancient shards and Dark totem parts. Hellhounds here are multicombat, safespottable, cannot be cannoned, and can reset aggression by running south and up the vine to the Giants' Den.
Xeric's Heart (Xeric's talisman) is beside the Catacombs entrance.
The Dagannoth are located in the southern section of the Catacombs of Kourend.
No dwarf cannon can be used, but the melee-only Dagannoth support prayer AFK and difficult safespots.

jormungand-s-prison-dagannoth.name: Jormungand's Prison
notes: Requires The Fremennik Exiles. The Dagannoth section is multicombat, cannonable, safespottable, and contains melee-only Dagannoth for straightforward Protect from Melee tasks.
Only accessible after completing The Fremennik Exiles.
Common location for cannoning Dagannoth.
Dagannoth here only use melee attacks, making Protect from Melee simple.

lighthouse-basement.name: Lighthouse Basement
notes: Requires Horror from the Deep. Multicombat Dagannoth area near fairy ring ALP; strong AFK and dwarf cannon option, often busy because it can provide very fast Slayer experience.
Usually busy with players using a dwarf cannon.
Can offer some of the fastest slayer experience in the game.
Good for maximising AFK time without relying on prayer.

waterbirth-island.name: Waterbirth Island
notes: Waterbirth Island Dungeon contains stronger Dagannoth, Dagannoth spawn eggs, and the Dagannoth Kings. Deeper areas require preparation such as a pet rock or Humphrey dumphrey plus a ranged weapon, rune thrownaxe, another player, or the 85 Agility shortcut.
Contains stronger Dagannoth than the other task locations plus 3 Dagannoth Kings deeper in the dungeon.
The entrance is not multicombat; reaching the multicombat zones normally requires a pet rock or Humphrey dumphrey and a ranged weapon or another player.
Trigger nearby eggs while Dagannoth remain aggressive to hatch dagannoth spawn and speed the task every few minutes.
A skeleton can be used to safespot north-east of the dungeon entrance after NPC aggression expires.
Reaching the Dagannoth Kings requires extra preparation.

dark-beasts.name: Dark beasts
notes: Dark beasts require 90 Slayer, 90 combat to be assigned, and starting Mourning's End Part II.
They can be killed with Melee, Magic, or Ranged, but Melee is the most effective style.
Use high prayer bonus armour such as Proselyte armour or Sunfire fanatic armour with Protect from Melee.
Dark beasts are permanently aggressive and do not become tolerant, so they can be killed with low attention once set up.
They only use Magic as their first attack if attacked first by the player, or if they cannot attack with Melee.
Night beasts require attention because their special attack fires three 3x3 magic hits based on current Hitpoints.
Bring a herb sack and gem bag to maximise profit from herb and gem drops.
Iorwerth Dungeon dark beasts can drop crystal shards.
Dark beasts and Night beasts are the only monsters that drop the dark bow and death talisman.
Dark beasts are useful point-gaining tasks because their base assignment size is small; Need More Darkness extends the task to 110-135.

Use melee with Protect from Melee and high prayer bonus armour. Cannon in Iorwerth Dungeon for crystal shard chance or Mourner Tunnels for Slayer ring access; bring herb sack, gem bag, seed box, and prayer sustain.

iorwerth-dungeon-dark-beasts.name: Iorwerth Dungeon
notes: Requires Song of the Elves. Contains 10 Dark beasts, is single-combat, supports a dwarf multicannon, is not safespottable for the task page, and Dark beasts killed here can drop crystal shards.
Dark beasts killed here have a chance to drop crystal shards.
Requires Song of the Elves for Iorwerth Dungeon access.
Use a dwarf multicannon, but expect single-combat kills.

mourner-tunnels.name: Mourner Tunnels
notes: Requires starting Mourning's End Part II. Contains 19 Dark beasts, is single-combat, supports a dwarf multicannon, and is easily accessed with a Slayer ring after completing Mourning's End Part II.
Easily accessed with a Slayer ring after completing Mourning's End Part II.
Can also be reached through the Death Altar via the Abyss, or through Mourner Headquarters.
Use a dwarf multicannon, but expect single-combat kills.

dark-warriors.name: Dark warriors
notes: Dark warriors are assigned only by Krystilia and must be killed in the Wilderness to count; there is no combat, Slayer or quest requirement.
slayerTargetId 256 is SYNTHETIC (C2/C3 allocation contract); the real SLAYER_TARGET varp value is a QA live-verify item.
The slayer-countable Dark warriors are the level 8 warriors of the Dark Warriors' Fortress (low-level Wilderness north-west of Edgeville).
They have huge melee defensive bonuses (stab +96) but zero magic and ranged defence, so magic or ranged is by far the fastest style.
No task extension unlock exists for Dark warriors.

Attack the level 8 Dark warriors in the Dark Warriors' Fortress with magic or ranged; their melee defence is very high (stab +96) but magic and ranged defence are zero. The fortress is low-level Wilderness, but bring risk-appropriate gear.

dark-warriors-fortress.name: Dark Warriors' Fortress
notes: The Dark Warriors' Fortress sits in the low-level Wilderness north-west of Edgeville; level 8 Dark warriors roam its corridors. Multicombat, cannon placement and safespots are not definitively wiki-stated, so conservative defaults are used. This is a PvP zone; bring risk-appropriate gear.
Level 8 Dark warriors roam the fortress corridors in the low-level Wilderness north-west of Edgeville.
Multicombat, cannon placement and safespots are not definitively wiki-stated; conservative defaults are used.

dogs.name: Dogs
notes: Dogs requires combat level 15 to be assigned by Turael, Spria, or Mazchna. There is no Slayer level requirement.
slayerTargetId 286 is SYNTHETIC (c2-c3-worklist section 1 allocation contract); the real SLAYER_TARGET varp value is a QA live-verify item.
The Dogs task counts guard dogs, jackals and wild dogs; each is a distinct monster with its own page (no single Dogs monster page exists, so wikiPageId is null).
Guard dog: combat level 44, 49 HP, max hit 5 (crush), Defence 37, no bonuses, no elemental weakness (npc 114/7209).
Jackal: combat level 21, 27 HP, max hit 3, Defence 15, 10% fire weakness (npc 4185/11583).
Wild dog: combat level 63, 62 HP, max hit 6, Defence 54, no bonuses (npc 112/113); highest Slayer XP.
None of the dogs are undead, so the salve amulet does not apply. No task extension unlock exists for Dogs.

Kill guard dogs in McGrubor's Wood (10 spawns) with any melee weapon, since none of the dog variants have defensive bonuses. Wild dogs in Brimhaven Dungeon give more Slayer XP; jackals in the Kharidian Desert have a 10% fire weakness that fire spells exploit for a Magic alternative.

dog-spawns.name: Dog spawns
notes: Dogs count guard dogs, jackals and wild dogs. Guard dogs are in McGrubor's Wood (10 spawns), Hosidius (6 spawns), Kourend Castle, Handelmort Mansion and Brimhaven (Heroes' Quest). Jackals roam the Kharidian Desert near Pollnivneach, Nardah, Sophanem and the Ancient Pyramid (largest cluster, 13 spawns, south of the Ancient Pyramid via fairy ring DLQ). Wild dogs are in Brimhaven Dungeon on Karamja (12 spawns). The Slayer task/Dogs location table (pageid 298041) lists every dog spot as cannonable and safespottable; only the Hosidius marketplace is multi-combat.
McGrubor's Wood holds the densest guard dog cluster (10 spawns); single-combat, so a cannon only hits one target at a time.

The Slayer task/Dogs wiki table (Hosidius marketplace, west of Nardah jackals, central Brimhaven Dungeon wild dogs, and Handelmort Mansion guard dogs) lists every dog location as cannonable and safespottable; Hosidius marketplace is the only multicombat spot.
Wild dogs (Brimhaven Dungeon, requires an axe) and jackals (west of Nardah, needs desert heat protection) are alternatives that also count as Dogs.

drakes.name: Drakes
notes: Drakes require 84 Slayer and 90 combat to be assigned.
They are found in the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon and require access to Mount Karuulm.
Before completing the Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary, wear boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots to avoid constant heat damage from the floor.
Drakes are draconic, so dragonbane weapons are very effective.
Drakes take 50% more damage from water spells.
Protect from Missiles fully blocks normal ranged attacks.
After seven auto-attacks, Drakes launch volcanic breath at the player's current position.
Volcanic breath deals 6-8 damage per hit for four hits without dragonfire protection, but can be reduced or negated with dragonfire protection or avoided by moving one tile.
Together, Protect from Missiles and dragonfire protection can let the player take no damage when attacking from at least one tile away.
Drake's claw and Drake's tooth upgrade boots of stone and holy sandals, and these drops are five times more common on a Slayer task.
Guardian Drakes can appear if superior monsters are enabled; their melee special can stun and hit heavily if the player does not move out of melee distance.
Most players tend to block drakes because they have high assignment weight, lacklustre drops, high stats, and flat armour despite being cannonable.

Use dragonbane melee or ranged with Protect from Missiles and dragonfire protection. Cannon the task-only Karuulm room, wear heat-protection boots unless Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is complete, and move one tile to dodge volcanic breath when not fully protected.

karuulm-slayer-dungeon-drakes.name: Karuulm Slayer Dungeon
notes: Drakes are on the middle level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon. Wear boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots unless Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary is complete. Use the task-only area for better cannon coverage in the smaller room.
Drakes are found on the middle level of the Karuulm Slayer Dungeon in Mount Karuulm.
The task page recommends the task-only area because the smaller room lets a cannon make better use of its shots.
Boots of stone, boots of brimstone, or granite boots are required before Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary protection.
The dungeon is accessible from Mount Karuulm teleports, fairy ring CIR, Battlefront Teleport, Skills necklace, or Farming cape routes.

requiredItems.name: Karuulm heat protection
requiredItems.waiverRequirement: Elite Kourend & Kebos Diary reward claimed

dust-devils.name: Dust devils
notes: Dust devils require 65 Slayer, 70 combat, and having started Desert Treasure I before they can be assigned.
A facemask, Slayer helmet, or Slayer helmet (i) is required; without protection, Dust devils deal rapid damage and drain Attack, Strength, Ranged, Magic, Agility, Defence, and Prayer stats.
Their attack is a ranged melee attack: it is considered melee and Protect from Melee works, but the accuracy roll uses the player's ranged defence.
Dust devils have very low Defence and a 35% air elemental weakness, while Choke devils have a 25% air weakness.
burst and barrage spells are the standard high-XP approach because Catacombs, Smoke Dungeon task-only, and Wilderness Slayer Cave locations support multicombat stacking.
Chinchompas and other area attacks can also be used, but Ancient Magicks is the task page's main equipment and method focus.
Catacombs of Kourend is highly recommended for most tasks because it is easy to reach, multicombat, and uses the Catacombs drop table.
Smoke Dungeon is quieter and has a large Dust devil population, but its task-only multicombat area cannot use a cannon while the single-way rooms can.
Wilderness Slayer Cave offers cannonable multicombat Dust devils and blighted supply options, but carries player-killer risk.
Choke devil superior spawns require the Bigger and Badder unlock and should be handled with the same facemask or Slayer helmet protection.
Killing a Dust devil in the Smoke Dungeon while wearing a Slayer helmet is part of the Hard Desert Diary.

Use a Slayer helmet or facemask and burst or barrage stacked Dust devils, usually in the Catacombs of Kourend. Use Smoke Dungeon for Konar locks or quieter task-only multicombat, remembering that the task-only area cannot be cannoned, and use Wilderness Slayer Cave only when accepting PvP risk or following a Krystilia assignment.

catacombs-of-kourend.name: Catacombs of Kourend
notes: Black demons here can be safespotted and give access to Ancient shards and Dark totem pieces, but their higher Defence makes them an inefficient Black demons task option. Mutated bloodvelds appear in three groups, can be safespotted, and use the Catacombs drop table including ancient shards and dark totem pieces. Brutal blue dragons here are safespottable, cannot be cannoned, and can drop ancient shards and Dark totem parts. Hellhounds here are multicombat, safespottable, cannot be cannoned, and can reset aggression by running south and up the vine to the Giants' Den.
Xeric's Heart (Xeric's talisman) is beside the Catacombs entrance.
The Catacombs of Kourend spot is multicombat, cannon-restricted, and the default recommendation for most non-Konar, non-Krystilia assignments.
Dust devils here use the Catacombs drop table, including ancient shards and dark totem pieces.
The area is easy to access and supports burst, barrage, chinchompa, and safespot play.

wilderness-slayer-cave-dust-devils.name: Wilderness Slayer Cave
notes: Dust devils are in the north-east Wilderness Slayer Cave area around level 25-28 Wilderness. The multicombat room can be cannoned, burst, barraged, and safespotted, but carries player-killer risk; do not bring items you are unwilling to lose.
The Wilderness Slayer Cave Dust devils are in level 25-28 Wilderness and are only relevant when assigned by Krystilia or when the player accepts PvP risk.
The multicombat layout allows cannoning and Ancient Magicks, and the monsters use the Wilderness Slayer Cave drop table.
Do not bring any items you are unwilling to lose; blighted ancient ice sacks can reduce rune costs.

smoke-dungeon-dust-devils.name: Smoke Dungeon
notes: Requires partial Desert Treasure I access and face protection from smoke effects and Dust devils. The task-only western multicombat area is guarded by Dusty Aliv and is good for bursting or barraging, but cannot use a dwarf multicannon; the remaining single-way rooms can be cannoned. Wearing a Slayer helmet here for a Dust devil kill is required for the Hard Desert Diary.
The Smoke Dungeon is remote and usually quieter than the Catacombs, with task-only multicombat Dust devils to the west guarded by Dusty Aliv.
The task-only western multicombat area cannot use a dwarf multicannon.
The remaining Smoke Dungeon Dust devil rooms are single-way combat and allow cannoning.

dwarves.name: Dwarves

Kill dwarves in the free-to-play Dwarven Mine beneath Ice Mountain (36 spawns) with any melee weapon; their Defence is trivial. Black Guards on Ice Mountain and in Keldagrim also count. Ranged is the better non-melee option, since dwarves carry a small +5 magic defence bonus.

dwarven-mine.name: Dwarven Mine

elves.name: Elves
notes: Elves require 70 combat and completion of Regicide before assignment.
Elves either use ranged or melee depending on their weapon; crystal bow users attack with ranged, while crystal halberd users attack with melee from up to two tiles away.
Until the player has access to Lletya, the only normal place to kill elves is Iorwerth Camp, which can be tedious to reach without an Iorwerth camp teleport.
Players who want to use a dwarf multicannon at Iorwerth Camp are discouraged because tents, barrels, and crates impede the cannon.
After enough Mourning's End Part I progress, players can kill elves in Lletya and level 108 Mourners downstairs in Mourner Headquarters.
Only level 108 Mourners downstairs count in Mourner Headquarters, and full Mourner gear must be worn for normal access; upstairs mourners and other levels do not count.
After Song of the Elves, players gain Prifddinas and Iorwerth Dungeon access; the dungeon contains 13 Iorwerth Warriors and allows cannon use.
Prifddinas guards and Iorwerth Dungeon warriors can drop crystal shards and enhanced crystal teleport seeds.
The task page recommends players skip elf tasks when possible because the task has lower weight from higher-level Slayer masters and the enhanced seed is rare.
Adept Reanimation on ensouled elf heads can be used as an alternative, giving 35 Slayer XP and 754 Prayer XP per reanimated elf.
Mourners at levels other than 108 do not count, and the elven traitor, Essyllt, and other elves fought during Song of the Elves do not count.

If completing the task, use melee with Protect from Melee or ranged/magic safespots. Iorwerth Dungeon after Song of the Elves is the best regular option because it has 13 warriors, cannon support, safespots, crystal shards, and enhanced crystal teleport seed access; Prifddinas guards are a convenient post-Song of the Elves alternative. Earlier accounts can use Lletya prayer altar/bank, Iorwerth Camp safespots, Mourner Headquarters before Song of the Elves, or Adept Reanimation for Prayer XP.

fire-giants.name: Fire giants
notes: Fire giants can be assigned at 65 combat with no Slayer level or quest requirement.
They are the strongest generic giants and are best known for rune scimitar drops.
All Fire giants have a 100% water elemental weakness; Branda the Fire Queen has a 50% water weakness through her Royal Titans profile.
Fire giants are aggressive, attack with slash melee, and are immune to weak burns.
Most Fire giant locations allow a dwarf multicannon; Catacombs of Kourend is the lone task-page exception, but it is multicombat.

Use Catacombs of Kourend for most tasks, prioritising level 109 Fire giants for better XP and Catacombs drops. Use Giants' Den when a cannonable Catacombs-table option is preferred, and use Konar-specific cannon locations such as Karuulm, Stronghold Slayer Cave, Waterfall, Isle of Souls, or Charred Dungeon when assigned there. fossil-island-wyverns.name: Fossil Island wyverns
notes: Fossil Island wyverns require 66 Slayer, 60 combat, Bone Voyage, and Elemental Workshop I before assignment.
They use melee and icy breath; several variants also use ranged or typeless magic.
Fossil Island wyvern icy breath requires an elemental shield, mind shield, dragonfire shield, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield to reduce damage.
The ancient wyvern shield is the only shield that grants immunity against the freezing effect from icy breath.
Protect from Magic can be used but only provides half the damage reduction of the listed shield protections.
Anti-dragon shield and antifire potions do not work to mitigate Fossil Island wyvern icy breath.
Fossil Island wyverns are draconic and are vulnerable to dragonbane weapons.
Spitting Wyverns are recommended for a quick clear because they are weakest and may use a weak ranged attack instead of icy breath.
Taloned Wyverns are the least favourable because their typeless magic attack is extremely accurate outside melee distance.
Long-tailed Wyverns should be engaged in melee distance with Protect from Melee active to avoid their typeless attack.
Ancient Wyverns require 82 Slayer and have better drops but much higher stats.
Many players buy Stop the Wyvern to block the task without using a blocklist slot because Fossil Island wyverns are not very profitable, do not give good experience, and are not ideal for points.
Wyverns may drop fossils of various sizes, and both caves have a Fossil Storage box by their entrances.

Use Spitting Wyverns for quick task completion, carrying an elemental, mind, dragonfire, dragonfire ward, or ancient wyvern shield for icy breath. Melee tank setups with high ranged Defence and Protect from Melee are the main strategy; use prayer gear, powered-staff Magic, or Ranged as alternatives. Avoid Taloned and Ancient Wyverns unless targeting their drops or accepting slower, harder kills.

wyvern-cave-fossil-island.name: Wyvern Cave (Fossil Island)
